chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Getting the Philadelphia club job through union agent Harry Marsh
summary: After Stuff he assembled a new group and, through drummer-union official Harry Marsh, got a job in Philadelphia that lasted two or three wartime years.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well now this group, you say, was after Stuff Smith, so this was after you'd left Stuff in
Yeah, because I came -- I got me another group since then, and went to Philadelphia, because I heard of a job over there, through a friend of mine, drummer, and --

Yeah, he was executive over there at the union, well, while he was delegate -- what you call it, business agent, and whatnot, and you know. He knew these people, and I went to see them, and I got the job.
I see. So -- what did you do? Did you tour with your own group for a while? How long did you have with this group?
Well, on tour, tour with my own group? No, no, No, I didn't tour. Well, Philadelphia.
Well mostly it was what? 52nd Street?
I stayed over there. I stayed in Philly, from -- from then to what? Oh, about three years, two or three years, I guess.
All during the war you stayed in Philadelphia. With your own group. I see.
